Note::sizes_view¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::span<const std::int64_t> Note::sizes_view() const

Inspect Geometry Without Allocating¶

sizes_view() returns a read-only span over the receiver’s extents. Its length equals dim(), and entry d equals size(d). A scalar therefore returns a valid empty span, a vector returns one extent, and a rank-three Note returns three. Zero extents are retained exactly, so shape [2, 0] remains distinguishable from [0, 2] even though both Notes contain no cells.

The span points into the Note’s implementation object. Calling the method is constant-time and allocation-free, but the span does not own that object. Do not retain it after the last Note sharing the implementation is destroyed or reassigned. Use sizes() when the extents need independent lifetime or mutation; that method returns a copied std::vector<std::int64_t>.

The elements are const, so callers cannot corrupt Note geometry through the view. Repeated calls on an unchanged Note refer to the same extent storage. Neither operation inspects text bytes. An undefined Note rejects rather than returning an empty span, because an empty span is already the valid shape of a defined scalar.

Example 1: Scalar Shape Is An Empty Span¶

const auto shape = pluss::note::make("alpha").sizes_view();
std::cout << "scalar=[] size=" << shape.size() << '\n';

Output¶

scalar=[] size=0

The empty span means rank zero, not absence and not zero cells.

Example 2: Read Matrix Extents¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 3});
const auto shape = grid.sizes_view();
std::cout << "grid=[" << shape[0] << ", " << shape[1] << "]\n";

Output¶

grid=[2, 3]

Example 3: Zero Extents Remain Visible¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 0});
const auto shape = empty.sizes_view();
std::cout << "empty=[" << shape[0] << ", " << shape[1] << "]\n";

Output¶

empty=[2, 0]

Example 4: Choose Borrowed Or Independent Geometry¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a", "b", "c", "d", "e", "f"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 3});
const auto view = grid.sizes_view();
const auto copy = grid.sizes();

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "view data stable=" << (view.data() == grid.sizes_view().data())
          << " copy independent=" << (copy.data() != view.data()) << '\n';

Output¶

view data stable=true copy independent=true

Use the span for immediate iteration or API calls that consume a span. Use the vector when storing shape beyond the receiver’s lifetime.

Example 5: Undefined Has No Geometry¶

try { (void)pluss::Note::undefined().sizes_view(); }
catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "sizes_view undefined: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

sizes_view undefined: rejected

See Also¶

  • sizes: return an owning, mutable copy of all extents.

  • size: query one axis with negative-axis normalization.

  • dim: return the number of extents.

  • vector: flatten cells while discarding their geometry.
